The lighthouse keeper, Elias, had spent forty years tending the light. One stormy morning, the sea delivered a bottle to his doorstep. Inside, a note: "To whoever finds this, I am stranded on the eastern shoal. Send help."

Elias knew the eastern shoal. It was a graveyard of ships. He radioed the coast guard, but the storm had knocked out communication. So he took his rowboat, braving the waves himself.

He reached the shoal. No one was there. Only a wreck, half-buried in sand, its hull torn open. He climbed aboard, searching. In the captain's cabin, he found a logbook. The last entry was dated fifty years ago. It read: "Sending a message in a bottle. If help comes, I shall be saved. If not, let this be my farewell."

Elias looked around. The cabin was untouched by time. Dust lay thick on the floor. No footprints but his own.

He understood then. The bottle had drifted for half a century. The captain had waited for a rescue that never came. Elias was too late—by fifty years.
